facts.text: Your cat's purr can literally heal you. It vibrates at a frequency that studies show helps heal bones and reduce pain, in you AND the cat.
Your dog can smell one hundred thousand times better than you. That's not an exaggeration, it's 300 million scent receptors doing the work.
Kittens from the exact same litter can have completely different fathers. It's called superfecundation, and it's more common than you'd think.
Why do dogs curl into a tight ball to sleep? It's an ancient survival instinct, conserving heat and protecting vital organs from predators.
Your cat spends a third of its entire life grooming itself. It's not vanity, it regulates temperature and hides scent from predators.
Your dog's nose print is as unique as your fingerprint. No two dogs on the planet share the same pattern of ridges and creases.
Cats can rotate their ears 180 degrees using 32 muscles, instantly pinpointing the exact direction any sound is coming from.
Newborn puppies are completely deaf and blind at birth. For their first couple weeks, smell and touch are all they have.
A cat's whiskers are almost exactly as wide as its body. That's the trick, it's how they instantly know if they'll fit through a gap.
Just making eye contact with your dog releases oxytocin, the same bonding hormone shared between mothers and their babies.
Why do cats' eyes glow in the dark? A hidden reflective layer called the tapetum lucidum sits right behind their retina.
Your dog might actually know exactly how long you've been gone. Their sense of time runs on how much your scent has faded.
Kittens start purring within days of being born, often while nursing, to signal contentment to their mother from the very start.
Some dogs can detect a seizure or blood sugar crash minutes before it happens, purely from subtle shifts in human scent.
Your cat's tongue is covered in tiny backward hooks called papillae, working like a hairbrush that scrapes meat clean off bone.
